subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: A KG1 child identifying basic body features such as head, eyes, nose, mouth, arms and legs.
altText: A Ghanaian KG1 child in a classroom pointing to their head and other body parts with a teacher nearby.
detailedDescription: A Ghanaian KG1 classroom where a child stands at the front, pointing to their head, eyes, nose and mouth as the teacher gently guides. Other children sit on a mat, watching and touching their own body parts while a simple body chart is displayed on the wall.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Children identifying body parts and what they are used for.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children pointing to eyes, ears, hands and legs while discussing what each body part does.
detailedDescription: Inside a KG1 classroom, a teacher shows a big picture of a child’s body with labels. Children point to their eyes for seeing, ears for hearing, hands for holding and legs for walking, linking each body part to its function in everyday life.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Children exploring front and back covers of a book and linking pictures to body parts.
altText: A teacher showing the front and back covers of a big book while KG1 children point to body parts in the pictures.
detailedDescription: A teacher holds up a large book and points to the front cover as children gather around. The cover shows a child’s face and body. On a table, the book is open, and children point to arms, legs and head in the pictures while learning about front and back covers of a book and connecting them to their own bodies.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: KG1 children using different body parts in action games and fine motor activities.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children jumping, clapping, walking on a line, hopping and threading beads to show body parts in action.
detailedDescription: In a lively KG1 classroom, a teacher leads a rhyme while some children jump and clap. One child carefully walks on a straight line on the floor to practise balance, another hops on one leg, and two children sit threading large colourful beads, showing hand–eye coordination and controlled use of body parts.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Children practising daily personal hygiene routines.
altText: A girl washing her hands with soap, a boy brushing his teeth and an adult combing a child’s hair at a school hygiene area.
detailedDescription: A neat washing area where a girl washes her hands with soap under a tap, while a boy brushes his teeth at a basin. Nearby, an adult gently combs a child’s hair. On the wall, a simple poster shows pictures of bathing, brushing teeth and washing hands to remind children of daily hygiene routines.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: A scene showing both a nuclear family and an extended family in a Ghanaian compound.
altText: A nuclear family in the foreground and an extended family on a veranda in a Ghanaian home, showing different family types.
detailedDescription: In the foreground, a father and mother help two young children get ready for school, representing a nuclear family. In the background on the veranda, a grandmother tells a story, an uncle helps a child with homework and an aunt braids a child’s hair, showing an extended family in a typical Ghanaian compound house.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: KG1 children matching picture cards of family members with their duties.
altText: Children in a Ghanaian KG1 classroom matching cards of family members doing chores with simple sentences.
detailedDescription: A KG1 classroom where the teacher stands by a chalkboard with picture cards of family members cooking, sweeping and fetching water matched with simple sentences. On the floor, small groups of children match their own picture cards and sentence cards that show mothers, fathers and children doing different home duties.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Teacher reading a storybook about a family and their roles to KG1 children.
altText: A teacher reading a big book on family roles while children describe what different family members do.
detailedDescription: A teacher sits on a low stool reading from a big book titled "Our Helpful Family". The open page shows a mother working and a father helping a child with homework. Children sit on mats, pointing at the pictures. Small speech bubbles show fathers cooking, mothers driving and grandparents gardening, as they talk about roles of family members.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: KG1 children identifying different parts of a home.
altText: A teacher showing a simple picture of a house while children point to rooms, compound and gate.
detailedDescription: A Ghanaian KG1 classroom where a teacher holds up a large picture of a house with labels. Children point to the bedroom, hall, kitchen, bathroom, compound and gate. Beside them is a small model or drawing of a simple family house to help them see the different parts of a home.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Children role-playing daily activities that take place in the home.
altText: KG1 children pretending to sweep, cook and bathe dolls in a dramatic play corner that looks like a home.
detailedDescription: In a classroom role-play corner arranged like a small home, one child pretends to sweep, another stirs an imaginary pot on a play stove, and a third washes a doll in a small basin. The teacher smiles and observes as children act out everyday activities done at home.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Teacher reading a story about a home while children relate it to their own homes.
altText: A teacher reading a storybook about a house to KG1 children who talk about similar things in their own homes.
detailedDescription: A KG1 teacher reads from a big book showing a family in their home. Children sit around, pointing to pictures of rooms and activities like cooking and sleeping. Some children lift their hands to share how their own homes are similar or different to the story home.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Children learning about safety rules in the home with help from an adult.
altText: An adult gently stopping a child from touching a dangerous object while other safe home behaviours are shown around.
detailedDescription: Inside a simple Ghanaian home, an adult kneels to gently stop a small child from touching a hot pot or electrical socket, calmly explaining the danger. Around them are examples of safety: toys packed away, a bucket pushed from the edge, and a closed gate. A small poster on the wall shows simple safety symbols to remind children how to stay safe at home.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Our World and Our People Curriculum (KG1)

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Children interacting with texts about families
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children and their teacher looking at a big book and picture cards about families during a picture walk activity.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, a teacher sits or stands with a large family-themed big book open on her lap or on an easel. Several children sit on a mat around her, pointing to the pictures of mothers, fathers, siblings and grandparents in the book. On a low table nearby, a few smaller books and picture cards show different family scenes. The classroom walls have simple posters and some children’s drawings. The scene shows learners interacting with texts about families and relating them to their own family experiences.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum: Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Family showing love and respect
altText: A Ghanaian family in their home compound showing love and respect as children politely talk to parents and help a grandparent.
detailedDescription: A warm Ghanaian home scene in a simple compound. A mother gently hugs or holds a young child who smiles back. Nearby, a father sits on a chair while an older child stands respectfully, speaking politely as if saying please or thank you. A grandmother or grandfather sits on a low stool and another child offers them a cup of water or helps them, showing respect. Two siblings share a toy or snack and smile together. Everyone wears simple Ghanaian-style clothes and their facial expressions clearly show kindness, love, and respect among family members.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum: Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: K1.1.4.1.1 – Physical features of the school
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children walking around their school compound and noticing features such as classrooms, office, canteen, toilet and playground.
detailedDescription: A bright Ghanaian school compound with a simple classroom block, a small office, a canteen or kitchen area, a toilet block and a playground. A teacher leads a group of KG1 children as they walk and point at the different features, learning that the school has many parts and each place has a purpose.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: K1.1.4.1.2 – Members of the school community
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children greeting and identifying the headteacher, teachers, school staff and classmates in a school compound.
detailedDescription: A Ghanaian school scene where KG1 children see different members of the school community. The headteacher stands near the office, a teacher talks with some learners, a cook or kitchen worker stands by the canteen, and a school caretaker works nearby. Children point respectfully and talk about who each person is and what they do, learning that many people work together to make the school safe and welcoming.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: K1.1.4.1.3 – Activities in the school
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children learning in class, playing outside and eating together to show different activities that happen in school.
detailedDescription: A lively Ghanaian school compound showing several activities at once: in one classroom, a teacher leads a lesson with children seated and answering; outside, another small group of learners play a simple circle game; nearby, a few children sit at a table sharing a snack. The scene shows that school is a place for learning, playing, eating and growing together as friends and future leaders.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: K1.1.4.1.4 – Interacting with texts about school
altText: A teacher reads a big book about school life to Ghanaian KG1 children who look at the pictures and talk about their own school.
detailedDescription: Inside a KG1 classroom, a teacher sits or kneels with a large storybook that shows pictures of classrooms, playgrounds and school friends. Children sit around her on a mat, pointing at the images and smiling as they connect the storybook scenes to their own school. The atmosphere is warm and thoughtful, helping children see reading as a tool for understanding their world and imagining better schools and futures.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: K1.1.4.1.5 – Safety in the school
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children and a teacher carefully avoiding a wet floor and a drain, showing how to stay safe in the school compound.
detailedDescription: A Ghanaian school compound where children practise wise and caring behaviour to keep everyone safe. One child gently stops a friend from running across a wet floor area being mopped, while a teacher shows two learners how to walk carefully near a low open drain or step. In the background, a child throws litter into a bin, helping keep the environment clean. The children look confident, thoughtful and protective of one another, modelling the mindset of future leaders who think before they act.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Living and non-living things in our environment
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children on a nature walk exploring plants, animals, and objects like stones and water to identify living and non-living things.
detailedDescription: A Ghanaian KG1 teacher leads curious children on a nature walk. Some pupils point to a small tree and a chicken, others to stones, a plastic bucket, and a puddle of water. The teacher encourages them to think, ask questions, and sort what they see into ‘living’ and ‘non-living’. The scene shows children as young explorers, observing and reasoning about their world, not just memorising lists.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Sorting living and non-living things
altText: KG1 children sort picture cards into living and non-living columns on a chart in a Ghanaian classroom.
detailedDescription: Inside a bright Ghanaian KG1 classroom, a large chart is divided into two columns labelled ‘Living’ and ‘Non-living’. Children work in small teams, discussing where to place picture cards of goats, trees, stones, balls, and buckets. The teacher guides them with questions like ‘Can it grow? Can it move by itself?’ so that pupils learn to think in terms of characteristics and not just copying the teacher’s answers.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Reading about living and non-living things
altText: KG1 teacher reading a big book on living and non-living things while children point to pictures and share ideas.
detailedDescription: A teacher sits with a big, colourful book titled ‘Living and Non-living Things’. The open pages show drawings of children, animals, plants, stones, and toys. KG1 learners sit in a semi-circle, pointing at pictures and explaining why they think something is living or non-living. Speech bubbles show their thoughts like ‘It grows’, ‘It does not eat’. The picture models a classroom culture where children connect reading with thinking, reasoning, and expressing their own ideas.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Exploring parts of a plant
altText: KG1 children examine a real potted plant and a simple chart showing roots, stem, leaves, flowers, and fruits.
detailedDescription: In a KG1 classroom, a real potted plant sits on a low table next to a simple wall chart labelling roots, stem, leaves, flowers, and fruits. Children gently touch the leaves and point to the matching parts on the chart. The teacher encourages them to observe closely and ask questions. The scene presents children as young scientists who are discovering how plants are built, not just memorising names.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Talking about uses of plants
altText: Children in a Ghanaian KG1 class discuss pictures of food, medicine, shade, and decoration that all come from plants.
detailedDescription: A teacher displays picture cards showing fufu, vegetables, herbal medicine, a shady tree, and flowers around a house. KG1 pupils link each picture to how plants help people: food, medicine, shade, and beauty. Some children point to a card and share how they use plants at home. The scene builds gratitude, practical thinking, and respect for nature as a partner in life, not just a resource to exploit.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Reading simple texts about plants
altText: KG1 children listen to a storybook about plants and point to pictures of roots, leaves, and fruits.
detailedDescription: A story-time scene where a teacher reads a big book on plants. The pages show a seed sprouting, a plant growing, and children harvesting fruits. Learners sit around, actively pointing to pictures and explaining what is happening. Their faces show curiosity and wonder, modelling a generation that can observe change, think in steps, and relate stories to real life and farming.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Caring for plants
altText: KG1 children water plants, weed around them, and avoid stepping on seedlings in a small school garden.
detailedDescription: Outside in a school garden, KG1 pupils water young plants with small containers, gently pull weeds, and carefully walk on the path instead of stepping on seedlings. A teacher praises them for protecting living things. The image trains children to see themselves as caretakers and problem-solvers for the environment, preparing them for future leadership in agriculture and stewardship.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Domestic and wild animals
altText: KG1 children sort pictures of domestic animals like goats and hens and wild animals like lions and elephants.
detailedDescription: In a KG1 classroom, a large chart is split into ‘Domestic animals’ and ‘Wild animals’. Children place picture cards of goats, sheep, hens, and dogs on one side, and lions, elephants, and monkeys on the other. The teacher invites them to explain why some animals live near people while others live in the wild, building early systems thinking about safety, responsibility, and our place in nature.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Imitating animal sounds and movements
altText: KG1 children happily imitate animal sounds and movements like meowing, barking, hopping, and flying.
detailedDescription: A playful circle-time activity where children act like animals: one hops like a frog, another flaps arms like a bird, another crawls like a lizard. They make gentle animal sounds while the teacher guides and laughs with them. The picture shows a safe space to explore imagination, empathy, and creativity—not just copying, but feeling how different creatures move in the world.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Reading and talking about animals
altText: KG1 teacher reads a storybook about animals while children point to pictures and share what they know.
detailedDescription: The teacher holds a big book full of colourful animals. Children point excitedly to a goat, a bird, and a lion as they listen to a simple story. They take turns sharing facts or experiences, like helping to feed goats at home. The scene supports confident communication and curiosity, training children to connect what they read with real life and their future roles as responsible caretakers of animals.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Showing kindness to animals
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children gently feed and give water to animals instead of throwing stones at them.
detailedDescription: In a neat school compound or home setting, children kindly feed goats and chickens, pouring water into a container and offering grains from a bowl. A teacher or caregiver smiles as one child stops another from throwing a stone. The image trains a heart-level value: leadership begins with how we treat weaker beings—animals, nature, and people around us.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Identifying different sources of water in the community.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children pointing to a tap, a rainwater barrel, a borehole and a nearby stream as sources of water.
detailedDescription: Outside a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, a teacher walks with a group of children and helps them notice different sources of water. One child touches a running tap near a small tank, another points to a covered rainwater barrel, and others look at a borehole pump and a stream in the background. The scene shows that water can come from many safe sources when communities plan well.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Talking about uses of water in daily life.
altText: KG1 children using water for drinking, washing hands, bathing a doll and watering plants with guidance from a teacher.
detailedDescription: In a school setting, KG1 children use water in different ways: one drinks from a clean cup, another washes hands at a handwashing station, a third child bathes a doll in a small basin during role play, and a group waters plants in a school garden. The teacher moves between them, asking why each use of water matters, so children connect water to health, cleanliness and growth.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Reading simple texts about water.
altText: A KG1 teacher reading a big book about water while children point to pictures of rain, taps, wells and children using water.
detailedDescription: Inside a KG1 classroom, learners sit in a semi-circle as their teacher reads a large storybook about water. The pages show rain falling, a tap running, a well with a bucket and children washing and drinking. Pupils point to the pictures and say what is happening. A small chart beside the board shows the word 'water' with a simple drawing, linking print, images and real experience.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Showing proper use and storage of water.
altText: KG1 children turning off a tap, pouring water carefully and covering buckets and containers to keep water clean.
detailedDescription: Near a school water point, a child closes a tap firmly after filling a bucket so water is not wasted. Another learner carefully pours water into a smaller container, and a third helps place a lid on a water bucket. A poster on the wall reminds them to save water and keep it covered. The picture teaches children that using and storing water wisely protects health and the environment.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Presence of air
altText: KG1 learners exploring the presence of air with balloons, pinwheels and a simple fan in a Ghanaian classroom.
detailedDescription: A KG1 class of Ghanaian children explore the presence of air through playful experiments. Some children blow air into balloons, others watch colourful pinwheels spin in front of a standing fan, and a small kite or cloth lifts as a child runs. The teacher kneels among them, asking questions and guiding them to notice that invisible air can push, fill and move things.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Uses of air in everyday life
altText: KG1 learners exploring everyday uses of air such as breathing, cooling with a fan, drying clothes, fanning a fire and flying a kite.
detailedDescription: In and around a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, children explore different uses of air. One child breathes deeply with a hand on the chest as the teacher talks about breathing, another stands in front of a fan enjoying cool air, a group watches clothes fluttering on a drying line, one learner gently fans a small charcoal fire while being supervised, and two children run with a paper kite lifted by the wind. The scene shows that air makes many everyday activities possible and useful.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Reading texts about air
altText: KG1 learners listening to a big-book read-aloud about air and using pictures and words to understand its uses.
detailedDescription: A KG1 teacher reads aloud from a big book about air while learners sit in a semi-circle. The pages show pictures of balloons, trees moving in the wind, fans and kites. Some children point to the pictures, some quietly mouth the key words on a simple word chart such as 'air', 'breathing' and 'cooling'. The teacher pauses to ask questions, helping learners connect the images, printed words and their real-life experiences.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Keeping our air clean
altText: KG1 learners practising ways to keep the air clean around their school, such as avoiding smoke, covering refuse bins and watering trees.
detailedDescription: Outside a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, small groups of children learn simple ways to care for the air they breathe. A teacher gently leads learners away from a smoking rubbish heap while explaining why burning rubbish near classrooms is harmful. Another learner helps close the lid of a refuse bin to stop bad smells and flies. Nearby, a small group waters a young tree planted near the school. The scene communicates that even young children can take responsibility for keeping their air clean and healthy.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: KG1 learners noticing different things in creation as gifts.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children and their teacher outdoors, pointing to the sun, trees, birds, water and hills as examples of creation.
detailedDescription: A Ghanaian KG1 class stands outside under a tree with their teacher. Children point to the bright sun, trees, flowers, birds, a small hill and a nearby stream or water container. The teacher encourages them to notice that all these beautiful things in nature are gifts. The image models a sense of wonder and gratitude for creation without focusing on any single religious group.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: KG1 learners talking about how God provides for their needs.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children in class and in the compound noticing food, clean water, rain and family as ways God provides.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian KG1 setting, children experience and discuss different ways their needs are met. Some sit at a table eating a simple school meal and drinking clean water, others walk with umbrellas in light rain, and a farmer in the background tends green crops. The teacher talks with them about food, water, rain and family as provisions, helping learners connect daily life with the idea that their needs are cared for. The focus is gratitude and responsibility, not fear.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Interacting with simple texts about creation.
altText: A KG1 teacher reads a big book on creation while children point to pictures of sky, land, plants, animals and people.
detailedDescription: Inside a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, a teacher holds a large storybook about creation. The open pages show pictures of the sky, land, plants, animals and people. Children sit in a semi-circle, pointing at the pictures and quietly sharing what they see. A simple word chart near the board shows words like sky, earth, plants and animals. The image models reading as a way to think, talk and learn about creation instead of just memorising words.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Showing appreciation to God through words, songs and actions.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children and their teacher taking a short moment to say thank you for life, food, family and school, with some drawing pictures of creation.
detailedDescription: At the end of a lesson, a KG1 teacher leads children in a short moment of appreciation. Some children gently join their hands, others quietly say thank you for life, family and school, and a few draw simple pictures of the sun, trees and houses on paper as a way of expressing gratitude. There are no heavy religious symbols; the focus is a peaceful heart attitude of thankfulness and joy.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Identifying good values and morals.
altText: KG1 children and their teacher matching picture cards of honesty, kindness, respect, sharing and helping to a values chart on the wall.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, a large chart on the wall shows simple pictures and words for values such as honesty, kindness, respect, sharing and helping. Children sit with their teacher, holding small picture cards like two children sharing a toy, a learner telling the truth, or a child helping another up. They match these cards to the correct values on the chart, learning that values are guides for how they treat people.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Practising good values in everyday situations.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children sharing, helping a friend, speaking politely to a teacher and resolving a disagreement with guidance.
detailedDescription: In a school compound, several small scenes show KG1 children practising good values. One child shares a snack with a friend, another helps a classmate pick up dropped books, another speaks politely to a teacher, and two children settle a small disagreement while the teacher gently guides them. The picture communicates that values like kindness, honesty, respect and forgiveness are lived out through daily choices and actions.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Interacting with texts that teach good values.
altText: A teacher reads a storybook about a child who returns lost money, while KG1 learners talk about honesty and what they would do.
detailedDescription: A KG1 teacher reads a big storybook that shows a child finding money and honestly returning it. Learners sit around on a mat, pointing to the pictures and listening. On a nearby chart, the word honesty is written with a simple symbol. Some children raise their hands to share what they would do in the same situation. The image shows that stories and texts are tools for thinking about values and making wise choices, building future leaders who can reason morally, not just obey rules.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: KG1 children visiting and talking about special places in their community.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children and their teacher walking past a school, clinic, police station and chief’s house, pointing and asking questions.
detailedDescription: A Ghanaian KG1 class goes on a short, safe community walk led by their teacher. They pass by special places such as the school, a small clinic or CHPS compound, a police station signboard and a chief’s house or palace. Children point, ask questions and share their own experiences of visiting these places. The teacher explains why each place is important to the community, helping learners see their local area as a living system they will one day help to improve.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Using pictures and simple texts to learn about special places in the community.
altText: KG1 teacher and learners doing a picture walk with a big book or poster showing places like the school, clinic, market and police station.
detailedDescription: Inside a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, a teacher holds a big book or poster with clear drawings of special places in the community: the school, clinic, market, police station and chief’s house. Children sit in a semi-circle and take turns pointing to the pictures as they talk about what happens in each place. The teacher uses before, during and after reading strategies to help learners connect illustrations, spoken words and their own experiences, making reading a tool for understanding and improving their community.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: KG1 children interacting with simple texts about national celebrations.
altText: A KG1 teacher and children looking at a big book and picture cards showing Independence Day, Farmers’ Day and other national celebrations, while learners talk about how people celebrate in Ghana.
detailedDescription: Inside a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, a teacher sits with a large storybook and picture cards showing scenes from national celebrations such as Independence Day parades, Farmers’ Day awards and cultural festivals. Children sit on a mat, pointing to pictures of people marching with flags, farmers receiving prizes and children in traditional dress. Some learners raise their hands to share what they have seen in their own community during such celebrations. On the wall, a simple chart shows symbols like the Ghana flag and a drum. The scene shows children interacting with texts about national celebrations and connecting them to their own experiences as young citizens.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Talking about neighbours, the work they do, and why their jobs matter.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children and their teacher in a community circle sharing about neighbours’ jobs like farmer, trader, nurse and teacher.
detailedDescription: The KG1 teacher leads a community circle time in a Ghanaian classroom. Children sit in a circle with picture cards showing neighbours’ occupations, such as farmers, traders, nurses, teachers, carpenters, fishermen and drivers. One child says, “My mother is a trader,” another says, “My father is a farmer.” The teacher writes simple job names on a chart and guides learners to see how each job helps the community. The scene builds respect for all honest work and helps children imagine their future roles.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Interacting with resource people from different occupations.
altText: KG1 learners dressed in simple job uniforms talking with a nurse, police officer, farmer and teacher visiting their classroom.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, resource persons from different occupations—such as a nurse, police officer, farmer and teacher—stand at the front, speaking to learners. Some children wear simple pretend uniforms made from paper hats, badges or aprons to show the jobs they dream of doing. On the board is a KWL chart where learners share what they already know and what they want to know about each job. They ask respectful questions and listen to the answers, building aspiration, confidence and a sense that they, too, can grow to serve their community.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Talking about traditional and religious leaders and their roles.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children with their teacher looking at posters of a chief, queen mother, imam and pastor, discussing how they help the community.
detailedDescription: A KG1 class in Ghana looks at posters or pictures showing special leaders: a traditional chief under an umbrella, a queen mother, an imam and a pastor. The teacher invites learners to describe who these people are and how they support the community—for example, advising people, settling disputes, praying, teaching and organising help for those in need. Some children role-play the leaders in simple, respectful ways. The picture teaches respect and understanding without fear or division, and helps children see leadership as service.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Listening to a read-aloud text about special leaders and how they support the community.
altText: KG1 teacher reading a big book about community leaders while children listen, point to pictures and share what they have learnt.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, the teacher reads an informational big book titled "Our Leaders". The pages show a chief, assembly member, headteacher, and religious leaders working to help their communities. Learners listen attentively, sometimes turning to a partner to say what they heard. After the reading, they share what they have learnt about the different ways leaders support the community. The scene models careful listening, reflection and respectful discussion.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Singing traditional songs, clapping, playing shakers and dancing together.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children singing a traditional song while some clap, others play shakers and a few dance in the middle.
detailedDescription: Under a shady tree or in a bright KG1 classroom, learners and their teacher sing a familiar traditional song from their culture. Half of the class claps the rhythm, a few learners play simple shakers, and some children take turns dancing in the centre. After the song, the teacher lets them talk about how they felt and why these songs are important. The image celebrates Ghanaian culture as joyful and living, helping children build identity, confidence and a sense of belonging.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Exploring different ways people communicate in Ghana and around the world.
altText: Ghanaian KG1 children and their teacher looking at objects like a radio, phone, letter, TV and computer to talk about how people share information.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, a low table displays picture cards and real or model objects such as a radio, mobile phone, letter envelope, simple computer or tablet and a small TV set. The teacher and children sit in a semi-circle. Each child takes a turn to pick an object or card and say how people use it to send or receive information. On the wall, a simple chart shows pictures and words like phone, radio, letter, TV and computer. The image presents communication tools as ways to learn, share ideas and stay connected, not just to consume entertainment.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Identifying different means of transportation and how they help people move.
altText: KG1 children matching picture cards of buses, taxis, bicycles, canoes and aeroplanes to a transport chart in a Ghanaian school.
detailedDescription: Outside on the school compound, a Ghanaian KG1 teacher stands beside a large chart showing different vehicles: a trotro or bus, a taxi, a bicycle, a canoe or boat and an aeroplane. Children hold small picture cards of people travelling and take turns matching them to the correct vehicle on the chart. On the ground, some learners play with toy cars, a toy bus and a toy plane on a simple road-and-sky play mat to act out safe journeys. The teacher asks where each vehicle might go and how we can travel safely, helping children see transport as a tool for visiting, learning, trading and serving others.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1

subject: KG1 Our World and Our People
caption: Using simple texts to learn about communication and transportation.
altText: A KG1 teacher reads a big book on how we communicate and travel while children point to pictures of phones, letters, buses and planes.
detailedDescription: Inside a Ghanaian KG1 classroom, the teacher reads from a large storybook or poster titled "How We Communicate and Travel". The open pages show children calling a relative on the phone, sending a letter, watching news on TV, sitting in a bus and seeing an aeroplane in the sky. Learners sit on a mat, some pointing to the pictures and others quietly looking at a nearby chart with simple word-and-picture pairs such as talk, call, travel and visit. After the read-aloud, two children stand to briefly act out calling a friend and travelling to meet them. The image shows texts as tools for understanding global connections and imagining positive ways to use communication and transport in the future.
sourceDocumentTitle: KG Curriculum – Our World and Our People KG1
